content.value_statement: Type assertions can hide incomplete or invalid test fixtures. This skill converts common assertions to Shoehorn helpers while preserving test intent and type feedback.
actual_capabilities: Guides searches for direct and double type assertions in TypeScript test files.
Maps direct assertions to the fromPartial helper for incomplete fixtures.
Maps double assertions to the fromAny helper for intentionally invalid fixtures.
Adds Shoehorn imports and identifies the required package installation step.
Explains when to use fromPartial, fromAny, and fromExact.
limitations: Targets TypeScript test code and explicitly excludes production code.
The suggested grep pattern may miss aliases, generics, lowercase types, or unusual formatting.
The skill does not define project-specific test or type-check commands.
Using fromAny intentionally weakens type checking for negative test data.

use_cases.title: Simplify Large Test Fixtures
use_cases.description: Convert partial request, response, or domain fixtures without fabricating every required property.

use_cases.title: Preserve Negative Test Data
use_cases.description: Replace double assertions used to create intentionally malformed values for negative tests.

use_cases.title: Standardize Fixture Patterns
use_cases.description: Standardize test fixture construction around explicit Shoehorn helpers during codebase cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Shoehorn Helper
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain when fromPartial, fromAny, and fromExact should replace TypeScript assertions in tests. Include one migration recommendation for [fixture type].
prompt_templates.scenario: Learn the available migration patterns before changing files.

prompt_templates.title: Review Test Assertions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review TypeScript test files in [path]. List each direct or double assertion and recommend the matching Shoehorn helper without editing files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Assess migration scope and confirm fixture intent.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate Selected Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Migrate assertions in [path] to @total-typescript/shoehorn. Add required imports, preserve intentional invalid data, and run the project's type check.
prompt_templates.scenario: Apply a focused migration to approved test files.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and Complete a Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [path] for unsafe test fixture assertions. Separate partial fixtures from intentionally invalid fixtures, migrate them, and summarize verification results and unresolved cases.
prompt_templates.scenario: Complete a broader migration with verification and exception reporting.

output_examples.input: Review the tests in the user service and recommend Shoehorn helpers.
output: Found six direct assertions and two double assertions in the selected test files.
Use fromPartial for incomplete request fixtures and fromAny for deliberately invalid identifier values.
No production files were included in the recommendation.

output_examples.input: Migrate the selected request handler tests and verify the result.
output: Replaced direct fixture assertions with fromPartial and added the required imports.
Preserved one malformed fixture with fromAny because the test validates an error path.
The project type check passed after the migration.

output_examples.input: Explain why one fixture should not use fromAny.
output_examples.output: The fixture is incomplete but otherwise valid, so fromPartial preserves useful property checks. Reserve fromAny for deliberately invalid test data.

best_practices: Confirm whether each fixture is partial or intentionally invalid before selecting a helper.
Limit changes to test files and keep Shoehorn out of production code.
Run the project type check and relevant tests after migration.
anti_patterns: Do not use Shoehorn in production code.
Do not replace assertions without checking the purpose of each fixture.
Do not convert intentionally invalid data to fromPartial; use fromAny and document the test intent.

faq.question: What problem does this skill solve?
faq.answer: It replaces TypeScript test assertions with explicit helpers for partial or intentionally invalid fixtures.

faq.question: Does the skill install Shoehorn?
faq.answer: The workflow includes npm installation, but installation should follow the repository's dependency policy and user approval.

faq.question: Can Shoehorn be used in production code?
faq.answer: No. This skill explicitly limits Shoehorn to test code.

faq.question: Which helper handles incomplete fixtures?
faq.answer: Use fromPartial when supplied properties should still type-check against a larger target type.

faq.question: Which helper handles deliberately invalid data?
faq.answer: Use fromAny when a negative test intentionally supplies a value that violates the target type.

faq.question: Will the suggested search find every assertion?
faq.answer: No. Aliases, generics, lowercase type names, and unusual formatting may require additional project-aware searches.
